Days Of The New.biography: Days of the New is an American rock band from Charlestown, Indiana, formed in 1995. The band consists of vocalist/guitarist Travis Meeks and a variety of supporting musicians. They are best known for the hit singles "Touch, Peel and Stand", "The Down Town", "Shelf in the Room", and "Enemy".

perplexity.description:
Days of the New (1997) marked the debut of Indiana rock band Days of the New, establishing the group's signature sound of dark acoustic rock with melodic sensibilities. Released on June 3, 1997, through Outpost Records, the album was recorded in October and November 1996 at Woodland Studios in Nashville under the production of Scott Litt, known for his work with R.E.M. and Nirvana. The twelve-track collection, informally known as the "Yellow" or "Orange" album after its cover design, showcased lead vocalist and guitarist Travis Meeks' songwriting and the band's fresh acoustic approach combined with catchy vocal hooks.

The album achieved substantial commercial success, selling 1.5 million copies worldwide and earning platinum certification in the United States. Three singles from the record became significant radio hits: "Touch, Peel and Stand" dominated Billboard's Rock Chart for 17 weeks and was later named the "Greatest of All-Time Mainstream Rock Song" by Billboard, while "The Down Town" and "Shelf in the Room" both achieved top 40 status. The album's relevance in 1997 stemmed from its distinctive positioning within the rock landscape—a departure from the prevailing grunge aesthetic that offered listeners an alternative through its acoustic-driven arrangements.

Despite the album's commercial triumph, internal tensions within the band emerged following a 1998 tour with Metallica and Jerry Cantrell. The original lineup disbanded in 1999, with most members forming the band Tantric while Meeks continued under the Days of the New name, recording subsequent self-titled albums in 1999 and 2001. The debut album remains the band's most commercially successful and critically enduring work, establishing the template for their acoustic rock sound that defined their early career.
